sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. No one appears on behalf of respondent no.2 despite service of notice.

3. The F.I.R. in question was lodged through an order passed on an application under Section 156(3)
Cr.P.C. on 23.1.2022 alleging that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicants and Lallan Sharma on 3.4.2021 for which a criminal case bearing 177/2021 was registered on 10.4.2021.

Subsequently, it was alleged that the aforesaid accused had beaten up the informant for which a separate case crime no.532/ 2021 was lodged on 13.11.2021 and thereafter on 26.11.2021,
the accused named in the F.I.R. caught hold of the daughter of the informant and stuffed some cloth in the mouth of the victim and thereafter wrong was committed by them upon the victim.
Ankul

1 4.

Learned counsel for the applicants has drawn my attention to the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein the victim stated that no wrong was done to her by Sudhir and Ankul except Ankit who has done wrong.
It was stated that Ankul has caught her legs.

Hence the applicants who are in custody since 10.6.2022 and have no criminal antecedents except the cases which has been duly explained in paragraphs 9 and 10 of the affidavit filed in support of the bail application,
may be enlarged on bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. also opposed the prayer for bail.

6. Considering the fact that the F.I.R. in question was lodged after about three months of he alleged incident, coupled with the fact that in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., no alelgation of offence under Section 376 Cr.P.C. were levelled against the applicant and the fact that the applicants are in custody since 10.6.2022 having criminal history of two cases which have been duly explained in paragraphs 9 and 10 of the bail application and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicants if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
7.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicants Ankul and Ankit be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.26 of 2022, under Sections 376-D, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5(g)/6 of the POCSO Act, Madhoganj, District Hardoi on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicants shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicants shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which they are accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 15.2.2024/Shukla  Ankul And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home, ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73510555/
